request.system: You are an expert in clinical classification systems.

messages.content:
ICD-10-AM is the Australian modification of the International Statistical Classification of Diseases and Related Health Problems, 10th revision. Its disease codes are arranged in chapters, and a three-character category is written as one capital letter followed by two digits. The letter indicates the chapter or block: A and B are infectious diseases, C is malignant neoplasms, D is other neoplasms and blood disorders, E is endocrine, nutritional and metabolic disease, F is mental and behavioural disorders, G is the nervous system, H is the eye and ear, I is the circulatory system, J is the respiratory system, K is the digestive system, L is the skin, M is the musculoskeletal system, N is the genitourinary system, O is pregnancy and childbirth, P is the perinatal period, Q is congenital malformations, R is symptoms and abnormal findings, S and T are injury and poisoning, and Z is factors influencing health status. The two digits narrow the chapter to a specific category, for example J44 is chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and N17 is acute kidney failure.

The principal diagnosis is the single condition established after investigation to be chiefly responsible for the patient's episode of admitted care. It is not the patient's most serious comorbidity, not the presenting symptom, and not the procedure performed.

Using that structure, assign the three-character ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category for the episode below. Choose the chapter letter first, then the two digits.

Hospital course:
Discharge Summary:

Patient Name: [REDACTED]
Gender: Male
Age: 61 years old
Admission Date: [REDACTED]
Discharge Date: [REDACTED]
Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Hospital Course Summary:

The patient was admitted to the hospital on [REDACTED] with progressively worsening shortness of breath, weakness and fatigue. The patient was diagnosed with aortic valve stenosis, hypertensive heart disease, coronary artery disease, and COPD.

During the course of the hospital stay, various tests were performed including cardiac catheterization and transthoracic echocardiography. These tests showed significant stenosis of the proximal and mid-left anterior descending artery, severe aortic valve stenosis with moderate insufficiency, an ejection fraction of 32%, and significant atherosclerotic burden in the ascending and descending aortas and aortic arch.

Based on the results of the tests, the patient underwent minimally invasive aortic valve replacement with a 27 mm·St. Jude Trifecta stented pericardial bioprosthesis under general endotracheal anesthesia. Standard monitors were used including cerebral oximetry. The procedure was completed without any complications. The postoperative TEE showed that the previously described aortic arch atheroma remained intact.

Following the procedure, the patient was monitored closely and his condition gradually improved. The patient did not experience any perioperative stroke events or other complications. The patient was discharged home in a stable condition five days postoperatively.

Upon discharge, the patient was advised to continue taking his medications for hypertension and high cholesterol as prescribed by his doctor. The patient was also advised to avoid smoking and other forms of substance abuse, and to follow a healthy diet and exercise regime. The patient was advised to follow up with his physician as recommended.

Answer in the form CODE: <letter><digit><digit>

text:
The principal diagnosis is **severe aortic valve stenosis with moderate aortic insufficiency**, which is nonrheumatic.

- **Chapter:** This is a circulatory system disease, so the letter is **I**.
- **What was chiefly responsible for the admission:** The patient came in with worsening shortness of breath and fatigue. Investigation showed severe aortic stenosis with moderate insufficiency. That valve disease was the reason for the definitive treatment, a minimally invasive aortic valve replacement with a bioprosthesis.
- **Other conditions are secondary:** Coronary artery disease (I25), hypertensive heart disease (I11) and COPD (J44) were also documented. They were not the main reason for this episode of care.
- **Category:** Nonrheumatic aortic valve disorders are classified to **I35**. The combined stenosis and insufficiency would be I35.2 at the fourth-character level. There is no documentation of a rheumatic cause, which would point to I06.

CODE: I35
